signals.text: Revenue grew 7% a year over 3 years vs 13% over 5: growth is slowing.
Profit compounded at -1% vs revenue at 7%: profits are lagging sales.
Operating margin compressed 992 bps in 3 years (32.0% → 22.1%).
Working-capital days lengthened by 15 days in 3 years (-11 → 4).
Over 5 years, operating cash flow was 110% of reported profit: profits are turning into cash.

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned whether the 15% volume growth target is too optimistic given subdued demand and ramping captive mines.
Analysts pressed management on persistent delays in completing key rail lines like Jharsuguda-Sardega.

business.summary: Coal India Limited is a Maharatna company that produces and markets coal, supplying primarily to the power sector as well as non-power sectors through long-term linkages, e-auctions, and bridge linkages.

guidance.statement: Coal India targets coal production of 838 million tons for next financial year.
guidance.quote: With that -- keeping that 838 million tons, one target is kept in the 850 million.

guidance.statement: CIL targets total capex of INR17,500 crores for the next financial year.
guidance.quote: It is almost INR17,500 crores. This year... It is INR16,500 crores, and INR1,000 crores more, INR17,500 crores.

guidance.statement: The company maintains its target to reach 1 billion tons of production in the future.
guidance.quote: 1 billion, we are on course.

guidance.statement: Employee cost is expected to decrease by around INR2,000 crores this year and continue downward.
guidance.quote: We are expecting this year, employee cost will be less than the last year to the tune of around INR2,000 crores. And it will continue

guidance.statement: E-auction volume is expected to be around 15% in the fourth quarter.
guidance.quote: Around it.

guidance.statement: Capex is expected to be around INR18,000 crores in FY26.
guidance.quote: In FY '26, it will be around INR18,000 crores.

delivered.statement: Achieved highest ever 9-month coal production of 531.90 million tons with 11% growth.
Reported highest ever 9-month PBT of INR31,937 crores and PAT of INR23,849 crores.
Achieved highest ever 9-month revenue from operations of INR1,04,914 crores, up 5%.
CIL achieved a capex of INR5,702 crores in the first 9 months.
Power dispatches reached highest ever 9-month figure of 454.03 million tons.
Market capitalization stood at INR2,31,719 crores as of December 31, 2023.

calls.tone: Confident on robust demand and volume growth, with expectations of moderating e-auction premiums.

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned the sharp decline in e-auction premiums compared to previous quarters.
Analysts pressed on the impact and tax implications of changing the stripping activity adjustment policy.
Analyst asked about the 8 to 9 million ton lag in SECL and whether the overall target will be met.
Questioned the jump in receivables from INR13,000 crores to INR17,000 crores despite excess inventory.

guidance.statement: We are progressing as per the target of 780 million tons this year.
guidance.quote: And as per the target of 780 million tons this year, we are progressing.

guidance.statement: BCCL target is 41 million tons this year.
guidance.quote: 36.18 million last year and 41 million this year we have to do.

guidance.statement: MCL target of 204 million will be ensured.
guidance.quote: And the Team MCL and Team Coal India quite sure that target of 204 million will be ensured.

guidance.statement: We expect e-auction volume for the second half of the year to be roughly 15% of production.
guidance.quote: 15% of production, you can say, roughly.

guidance.statement: By this year-end, 250 megawatts of solar power we will be doing out of 3,000 megawatts target.
guidance.quote: So by this year-end, 250 megawatts we will be doing out of these 3,000.

guidance.statement: Capex as a whole for Coal India is INR16,500 crores.
guidance.quote: So capex as a whole for Coal India, it is INR16,500 crores.

guidance.statement: Production target for FY25 is 840 million tons.
guidance.quote: our production target for FY'25 is 840 million tons.

guidance.statement: Employee cost for the total volume is about INR46,000 crores.
guidance.quote: So about INR46,000 crores is the employee most of the total volume.

delivered.statement: H1 results showed strong production, dispatches, and overburden removal.
Overall e-auction premium over notified price was 90% for Coal India as a whole.
H1 offtake reached 360.66 million tons, with power sector taking 295.36 million tons.

calls.tone: confident on demand and production targets, focused on evacuation and execution efficiency

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned flat volumes at MCL and long-term growth plans.
Skepticism on achieving aggressive annual volume growth given current monthly run rates.
Inquiries regarding rake shortages and infrastructure readiness in SECL and MCL.

guidance.statement: The company is confident of achieving the 700 million tonnes production target this year.
guidance.quote: The company is quite sure that this year, we will be achieving the target of our 700 million tonnes.

guidance.statement: E-auction volume is expected to end the year around 80 million to 90 million tonnes.
guidance.quote: we will end the year with about 80 million to 90 million tonnes of e-auction coal.

guidance.statement: Targeting 1 billion tonnes production by FY25 or the year after.
guidance.quote: perhaps by FY25, we will reach something higher than 900 million tonne, and the year after, definitely it will be achieved.

guidance.statement: CAPEX is expected to reach Rs. 16,500 crores this year.
guidance.quote: this year we’ll reach Rs.16,500 crores.

delivered.statement: Meeting the demand of the power sector and maintaining supply to non-power.
Cost per tonne reduced significantly due to increased production.
Profitability increased due to higher e-auction prices and production.

calls.tone: Confident on meeting production targets and demand, cautious on wage negotiation impacts and regulatory pricing.

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned if potential government policy actions or windfall taxes pose risks to high e-auction prices.
Pressed on what drove the jump in receivables from Rs. 11,000 crores to Rs. 14,000 crores in Q1.
Scepticism on whether India and Coal India can realistically become self-sufficient in coking coal.

guidance.statement: CIL has envisaged a coal supply target of 850.24 MT in FY 2026-27.
guidance.quote: CIL has envisaged coal supply target of 850.24 MT in FY 2026-27 which is a growth of more than 14% over the previous year’s achievement.

guidance.statement: CIL has a strategic coal production roadmap targeting ~1BT by FY 2029-30.
guidance.quote: CIL has revised its coal production programme and a strategic coal production roadmap i.e. ~1BT by FY 2029-30.

guidance.statement: CIL planned a capital investment of Rs 16,500 Crores for FY 2026-27 and beyond.
guidance.quote: CIL has planned a capital investment of H 16,500 Crores for maintaining its volume growth in FY 2026-27 and beyond.

guidance.statement: CIL targets building 9.5 GW of renewable energy capacity by FY 2029-2030.
guidance.quote: We have set an ambitious target of building 9.5 GW of renewable energy capacity by FY 2029-2030

guidance.statement: The share of SILO loading is expected to grow up to 39% in FY 2026-27.
guidance.quote: The share of SILO loading is expected to grow upto 39% in the FY 2026-27.

guidance.statement: Total mechanised and rapid loading capacity is projected to reach 994 MTY by FY 2028-29.
guidance.quote: Upon completion of all FMC projects, CIL’s total mechanised/rapid loading capacity is projected to reach 994 MTY by FY 2028–29.

guidance.statement: CIL committed to achieving 3,000 MW of solar capacity by FY 2027-28 as part of its internal net-zero target.
guidance.quote: The company has committed to achieving 3,000 MW of solar capacity by FY 2027-28 as part of its internal net-zero target.

delivered.statement: Revenue from operations for FY 2025-26 stood at Rs 1,68,400 Crores.
Profit After Tax for FY 2025-26 was Rs 31,071 Crores.
EBITDA for FY 2025-26 reached Rs 53,276 Crores.
Total capital expenditure in FY 2025-26 was Rs 19,607 Crores.
Total dividend payout recommended for FY 2025-26 is Rs 26.50 per share.
Renewable energy capacity established reached 357.65 MW.

calls.tone: Confident and resilient, focused on energy security, execution efficiency, and long-term diversification into clean energy and gasification.

business.summary: Coal India Limited is a state-owned coal mining corporate producing the bulk of India's coal, while expanding into power generation, renewable energy, battery storage, and coal gasification.

credibility.line: Management consistently misses aggressive production and e-auction targets while capex climbs. Treat volume roadmaps with caution.
